title: The Birth of Thickets
extracted_text:
The Birth of Thickets
An Interregnum in Space
The legibility regime runs one operation. It converts Space into Place, and everything else it does follows from that.
Space is the undifferentiated field. It holds every possibility and offers no orientation, which is why standing in it feels less like freedom than like vertigo. Draw a boundary around part of it, name what is inside, and you have made a Place. A farm is a Place; beyond the fence is forest. Drawing that boundary is the first act of thought, because you cannot know anything you have not first cut out from everything else. The trouble begins when the operation runs everywhere, on everything, at once, until it stops being thought and becomes weather.
The Modernity Machine ran it at that scale for four centuries, always to the same pattern: take the living thing, name it, standardize it, and ship it somewhere it did not grow. The rubber tree becomes a cog expected to perform identically wherever it is planted, and then the plantation dies of its own tidiness. What four centuries of that produced is the terraformed plain, a landscape the map has already predicted and optimized, where the only way to move is the way the map allows. It is the habitat of the tourist.
Today, putting an idea into the world costs five orders of magnitude less than it did a millennium ago, and the cost of naming, summarising and ranking fell with it until it became free, and often negative. Anything you can say, a model can summarise, and what it summarises it averages. Give a hundred people the same model and each of them improves while the range of approaches collapses: everyone performs well, nobody goes sideways, and the group ends up reasoning worse than it did when its members were all wrong in different directions. Ideas arrive pre-commodified now, the same one surfacing in a dozen heads in the same week with no originator and no common knowledge among the people holding it, several of whom set off chasing an advantage that is already gone.
So the plain has reached back to the moment of having the thought. Two machines are working that ground at once, and the confusion between them explains a great deal. The Modernity Machine is in its Dusk, which does not mean it has gone: a machine in Dusk keeps its apparatus and loses its future. Most of the world’s energy still moves through it, and the reflex to name a thing so that it can be ranked is the part that runs longest. The Divergence Machine has held the Day since about 2000, and it pushes where the old one pulled, scattering people into separate realities instead of drawing them toward a single canonical direction. Which means the flattening you feel is not the work of the machine now in charge. Divergence supplies the material, and the old apparatus, still running, reads it back into something it can index.
The obvious answer would be to leave. You go somewhere else and build: twelve people convened around privacy, a charter, a members’ channel. But you have made a Place, and a Place is what the operation eats, so the plain will absorb it by the end of the quarter. The reflex is old and hard to see from inside. Grow a new shell quickly, armor up, become legible again. Resistance organised as an institution is only the regime with better intentions.
The escape runs instead through the thicket: Space that declined to convert. Its shape is a portal of curated Places opening onto an interior that stays open, and a shared vocabulary or a way of arguing is what those Places are made of. They are real, and they are the fence rather than the point. Mistake the fence for the interior and you fall into container metaphysics, the belief that the anchor is the goal, at which point you stop exploring and the thing you built settles into another tidy square on the plain. The interior has to stay high-entropy, because averaging needs nothing more than an inside orderly enough to summarise.
Keeping an interior open ought to cost something, and under the map it always does. Place is security, Space is freedom: once you are visible you have to choose between bounded and protected or open and exposed, and you pay for whichever you did not pick. Drop below the map’s resolution, though, and the choice does not get split. It stops being available. A regime extracts from what it can see and constrains what it can name, and inside a thicket it can do neither, so security and freedom stop behaving like opposite ends of one axis and arrive together as one property. Both words were only ever naming the same condition: not being handled.
The Dark Forest Theory of the internet suggests something similar, but I propose that the condition is a counterfeit, and easy to mistake for the real thing. The dark forest is a Place dressed as Space. I have described that retreat before as a return to the village, but a village built inside a bunker: hidden, bounded, unfree, with someone always at the door counting who goes in. A member-owned working group and an influencer’s private channel present identical surfaces, both opaque to outsiders, both thick with in-jokes, both perfectly clear about who belongs. What separates them is the direction the energy flows. Who pays the energy cost, and who captures the value? In the working group the energy stays with the people spending it. In the channel it is harvested out to the one person who owns the door, and what he hands back is neither freedom nor security. The platform runs that operation at scale, a container that promises you a world of your own and returns a legible slice of everyone’s, which is what the Dusk apparatus produces when it gets hold of divergence.
The Day Machine cut a new niche out of that same excess, the way the machine before it was undone by its own success at counting. While averaging is partial, illegibility is a luxury and a mild handicap: you give up reach to keep your shape. Once averaging goes total, illegibility becomes the only ground on which a shape can still stand, and people have started living on it. Liveness is the machine at Dawn. Nobody builds a Dawn machine; it turns on wherever something has begun running that the older logic cannot get hold of, and that is happening inside thickets. Whatever the next era turns out to be, its first working parts are running there now.
Thing is though, you cannot start a thicket, because founding is the operation. Write a charter, draw a boundary, keep a roster, and each of those acts converts Space into Place, so a thicket founded on purpose resolves quickly in favour of the plain. Decline to convert and what remains is a thicket. Allow the fence to rot, and what grows in the clearing is not something you planted.
So it arrives as a calling. The niche opens, some fascination you cannot put down turns out to fit it, and what hears the call is The Octotypic Mind: the distinct terroir of minds. Nobody convened the people who could not leave the dying web alone. The web began dying, which opened a niche for a kind of attention that had nowhere else to go, and the people already shaped for it walked in without ever deciding to.
Interregnums are usually described in time. The old machine is dying, the new one cannot yet be born, and what breeds in the interval is morbid: rulers who have stopped making sense, rulebooks growing faster than anyone can read them, institutions elaborating themselves well past the point of use. Monsters, in the oldest sense of the word, which meant an omen that something had gone wrong. But an interregnum in time can be swapped for an interregnum in space. You do not have to wait out the gap if you can go and stand where it has already closed, and that is what the habitat offers over the calendar.
A second kind of monster is waiting there. In the folkloric sense a monster is not evil, only reality reworking itself, the unfinished business of a world that was never fully articulated. It shows up where a form holds more possibility than it can contain and the form gives way. What opens is a crack, and a crack is not a gap or a lack or a hole wanting to be filled. It is surplus.
So the same excess sorts two ways. Read back into an index by the old apparatus, it turns morbid. Left unread, it splits the form and what comes through reworks whatever it touches. You cannot live inside a crack, since nothing keeps its shape at that range. You can only build alongside one, and thicketing is exactly that: staying near enough to be reworked, sheltered enough to survive it, and declining every invitation to say what the opening is for. The people who manage this tend to seem slightly monstrous and roaring with Liveness.
As with life, Liveness breaks rules. A Day is supposed to last four centuries, and machine lifespans have been shortening for as long as there have been machines to measure. Liveness is switching on inside thickets faster than the framework’s clock allows for, which would make the era only now beginning a short one, and would bring the Divergence Machine to its own Dusk well before the four centuries are up.
A thicket cannot be your target. Thicketing is the act of noticing, dwelling, and thriving in an emergent niche. But you don’t build a thicket; you give attention to the arrangement of the universe that has opened up a Space.
Coda #
The Space and Place vocabulary, and the formula place is security, space is freedom, come from Yi-Fu Tuan’s Space and Place: The Perspective of Experience (1977). The wider project this essay sits inside is spatial epistemology, knowing as a spatial act, and the Place-series that builds the vocabulary runs through Thinking with Places, Problems are Places, Questions are Spaces, The Shelter as Epistemic Engine, and We Need Homes in the Delta Quadrant.
The structural move at the centre of this essay is Bayo Akomolafe’s, from The Untimely, a talk he gave to the Long Now Foundation on 5 May 2026. His argument runs on time rather than space: the untimely is not an alternative clock but the interval the clock cannot count, the excess the machinery secretes by running. To create an alternative, he says, is to repeat the logic of what you are escaping from; sanctuary is not something you can schedule and build, but what the world conspires to make with the cracks in us. I have run the same operation on the other axis. He escapes through time; I have tried to escape through space, taking his structure and declining his fatalism, since the niche opens without you but occupying it is work.
The world-machines framework (the Modernity Machine, the Divergence Machine, the Liveness era, and the Dawn, Day and Dusk phases a machine passes through) is Venkatesh Rao’s, and this essay assumes familiarity with his Contraptions writing on the topic, in particular The Divergence Machine. Two moves here are mine rather than his. Reading the platform as a Dusk-phase legibility apparatus processing Divergence output runs against his account, in which divergence brackets modernity and renders it irrelevant rather than being recaptured by it. And the framework’s table gives the Divergence Machine a Day lasting to 2400, which the closing wager declines to believe.
The interregnum, and monsters as the morbid symptoms that breed in it, are Rao’s, from The Gramsci Gap (Contraptions, 11 January 2025), which also supplies the move this essay turns on: that an interregnum in time can be replaced by an interregnum in space. His monsters there are strictly pathological and want exorcising. The generative sense is Akomolafe’s, from I, Coronavirus. Mother. Monster. Activist. (15 May 2020) and from interviews where he defines a crack as life in excess of itself, too much possibility abiding in a form for the form to hold it, and the monster as reality reworking itself. The trickster who straddles worlds and upsets every enterprise of closure is his too. Rao arrives somewhere adjacent a year after the Gap essay, in Engineering Liveness (Contraptions, 31 January 2026), where slightly monstrous people carry unseemly levels of liveness. Reading the two senses as one excess sorted two ways is mine, and neither of them makes that claim.
Pre-commodified is Sachin’s, from “LLMs Pre-Commodify Ideas” (Summer Lightning, 12 June 2026): when enough people work the same latent space, an idea surfaces everywhere at once and arrives already commodified, so that provenance rather than origination becomes the scarce thing.
The thicket is from my own The Architecture of Resistance, and the trilogy it belongs to runs from Logic of the Thicket and the Unsearchable Web through that essay to The Deep Dark Terroir of the Soul. The cost-collapse argument is from The Lightening of Intent, and Not My Lever promised this essay.
